etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tough, towgh, tou, toȝ, from Old English tōh (“tough, tenacious, holding fast together; pliant; sticky, glutinous, clammy”), from Proto-West Germanic *tą̄h(ī), from Proto-Germanic *tanhuz (“fitting; clinging; tenacious; tough”), from Proto-Indo-European *denḱ- (“to bite”).

definitions.definition: (of a material) Strong and resilient; sturdy.
(of food) Difficult to cut or chew.
(of a person or animal) Rugged or physically hardy.

quote.citation: 2010, Brian Lovett, Hunting Tough Turkeys, Stackpole Books, page 3:
quote.text: But before you quit turkey hunting and take up model-train collecting, let me give you the good news: you can score on tough turkeys. In fact, you can kill the toughest turkey in the woods.

definitions.definition: (of a person) Stubborn or persistent; capable of stubbornness or persistence.

definitions.definition: (material science) Undergoing plastic deformation before breaking.
